replacement_spec.body: The spectral centroid is a human-made measure used in signal and audio processing that quantifies the center of mass of a spectrum's magnitude distribution — the point at which the energy of the spectrum would balance if it were a physical object. It is computed as the weighted mean of the frequency components, where the weights are the magnitudes at each frequency, and is typically expressed in Hertz. The spectral centroid serves as a proxy for the perceptual attribute of brightness in sound, since higher centroids correspond to more high-frequency energy. It is a scalar descriptor extracted from a single spectrum frame and is widely used in audio analysis, instrument recognition, and music information retrieval. e.g.: spectral centroid of a musical note computed by a Short-Time Fourier Transform; spectral centroid used to distinguish bass from treble timbre in a music information retrieval study; spectral centroid of a speech formant band measured in Praat for voice quality analysis | not: spectral-band-centroid (a centroid computed within a sub-band, not the full spectrum) [formal: centrum spectrale | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes]
